name: Marine Conservation & Reef Monitoring Field Program

seo.title: Marine Conservation & Reef Monitoring Field Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Two weeks on Oʻahu: earn your PADI Open Water and Ecological Monitoring Program certifications, survey coral reefs, join conservation projects, surf the North Shore. Ages 17–22.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Scuba & reef monitoring certifications
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Honolulu for orientation, then spend three days earning your PADI Open Water Diver certification, learning essential dive skills and completing open-water dives.

Next you begin the Ecological Monitoring Program with Ocean Alliance. Each day starts with a classroom session on topics such as coral reef ecology, invertebrate population management and Hawaiʻi fish identification, followed by dives where you practice buoyancy and conduct underwater surveys.
weeks.imageAlt: Scuba diver writing on a slate while swimming over a reef

weeks.title: Service, surf & Shark’s Cove
weeks.body:
The monitoring program wraps up with substrate composition, using photogrammetry to build 3D models of reef structures. Two days of service learning follow with local organisations such as Papahana, the Aloha Tree Alliance and Mālama Maunalua, from native tree planting to removing invasive algae in Maunalua Bay.

Then we head to Haleʻiwa on the North Shore for two days of surf lessons and exploring, snorkel at Shark’s Cove and wrap up the program before flying home from Honolulu.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Medium activity level. Anyone with an average fitness level and an enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect daily diving during the certification and monitoring program, surf lessons, snorkeling and some physical work on volunteer projects, like removing invasive plants.

items.title: Conservation Diver Ecological Monitoring Program
items.body: Classroom sessions and research dives covering coral reef ecology, invertebrate population management, fish identification and substrate composition, with photogrammetry of reef structures. You earn the Conservation Diver Ecological Monitoring Program Certification on successful completion.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: Do I need to know how to scuba dive?
items.a: No. You’ll spend three days earning your PADI Open Water Diver certification before the Ecological Monitoring Program begins.

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No. Surf lessons on the North Shore are for first-timers and for those looking to sharpen their skills.

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: The program suits anyone of average fitness with an enthusiasm for the outdoors. Expect daily diving in the first week, surf lessons and snorkeling, and some physical work on volunteer projects.
In clean group accommodation: hostels in Waikiki and Haleʻiwa, and yurts at Sun Farm. There’s no camping on this program.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover flights to and from Hawaiʻi, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
